bull.b: Strong revenue growth combined with very high gross margins indicates attractive product economics and expanding commercial traction. If sustained, this mix can support reinvestment in sales, launches, and market access while creating a foundation for improved operating profitability over the next several quarters.

The shift to positive operating and free cash flow strengthens near-term liquidity and demonstrates that cash generation is improving faster than reported net income. Sustained conversion would give Harrow more capacity to fund products and reduce reliance on external financing.

TYRVAYA broadens Harrow’s dry-eye portfolio with a complementary, drop-free therapy and adds experienced commercial personnel. Combining it with VEVYE can increase the products offered per physician relationship, deepen category presence, and create a larger platform for future ophthalmic growth.

bear.t: Elevated leverage and thin equity cushion
bear.b: Higher leverage and minimal equity reduce financial flexibility if operating performance weakens. Debt-funded asset growth increases refinancing exposure, while the limited equity cushion can constrain investment choices and heighten the potential impact of future funding needs.

Widening losses show that strong product-level margins have not yet translated into dependable company-wide earnings. Elevated operating costs or non-operating pressures may continue to absorb gross profit, making sustainable profitability dependent on revenue scale and disciplined expense management.

bear.t: Execution risk from required second-half ramp
bear.b: Meeting full-year guidance requires a substantial acceleration from the first half, increasing dependence on VEVYE growth, IHEEZO channel normalization, salesforce productivity, and TYRVAYA integration. Higher SG&A and acquisition-related spending add execution pressure before the expected benefits fully materialize.
